overview: Both muscle types are striated, but cardiac muscle is involuntary and uniquely built for continuous, rhythmic contraction.
genZNote: Cardiac muscle: striated but works on autopilot, never taking a break. Skeletal muscle: striated and under your direct control.

aspects.label: Type of Control
aspects.valueA: Involuntary — contracts automatically, without conscious control.

aspects.label: Nucleus per Cell
aspects.valueA: Usually single, centrally located nucleus (uninucleate), with branching fibres.
aspects.valueB: Multiple nuclei per cell (multinucleate), with unbranched fibres.

aspects.label: Special Structural Feature
aspects.valueA: Contains intercalated discs connecting adjacent cells, allowing coordinated contraction.

aspects.label: Fatigue Resistance
aspects.valueA: Highly resistant to fatigue — must work continuously throughout life.
aspects.valueB: Fatigues relatively quickly with sustained heavy use.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Intercalated discs in cardiac muscle allow electrical signals to pass rapidly between cells, letting the heart contract as a single coordinated unit.
overlay.memoryTrick: Both are striated, but cardiac = involuntary and tireless; skeletal = voluntary and fatigable.
overlay.commonMisconception: Cardiac muscle is not simply 'smooth muscle with stripes' — it's a genuinely distinct third muscle type with its own unique cell structure (intercalated discs, branching).
